claim: DP hours explain a moderate share of chess rating variance: about 26% in the Games meta-analysis (r=.51, 11 effect sizes) and about 18% in Gobet and Campitelli (r=.42).
agent_test: Not testable on the agent directly; sets the prior that practice amount is necessary but far from sufficient.

claim: Chess DP explains roughly one third of reliable variance (34%) after reliability correction, so about two thirds stays unexplained by DP hours.
agent_test: Treat any practice-scaffold gain as partial; always compare to a no-practice control at equal tokens.

claim: Variance explained depends on how DP is measured: log 5%, questionnaire 12%, interview 20%; reliability correction raises overall r from .38 to about .43-.63.
agent_test: Measure agent practice with logged counts, not self-report; report corrected and uncorrected effects.

claim: The Ericsson 1993 violin 'best > good' gap did not replicate: best M=8224 h vs good M=9844 h (t(24)=-0.93, p=.364); only good vs less accomplished differed (d=1.33).
agent_test: Check that top-tier agent performance is not explained by raw token volume alone: compare tiers at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Practice effects are domain-dependent: games 26%, music 21%, sports 18%, education 4%, professions <1%; stable, predictable domains show more (24% high vs 4% low predictability).
agent_test: Measure scaffold gain separately on predictable (rule-fixed puzzle) and unpredictable tasks.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Among elite performers practice explains little (sports elite 1%); range restriction and ceiling effects are argued both ways (Ericsson and Harwell dispute the correction).
agent_test: Test whether scaffold gains shrink on tasks where the baseline is already near ceiling.

claim: Fluid intelligence matters more for lower-skilled chess players than for higher-skilled ones (Burgoyne 2016); only seen second-hand.
agent_test: Vary base-model strength and see whether scaffold benefit is larger for weaker models.

claim: Starting age predicts chess skill beyond accumulated DP (Gobet and Campitelli 2007; Howard 2012).
agent_test: Background only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Individual differences in hours needed to reach master are large: 3,016 to 23,608 h (about 8-fold).
agent_test: Expect large run-to-run variance in agent learning; use many seeds.

claim: Solitary study is the best DP predictor in chess; playing games adds no reliable benefit once solitary study is controlled (Charness 2005), but its inclusion is disputed by Ericsson.
agent_test: Compare self-play-only vs targeted-study-only agent loops at equal tokens.

claim: Large Chess.com longitudinal data (N=44,213): DP-aligned activities had 3.61x learning efficiency vs gameplay, though over 90% of time went to games; not all DP activities equal.
agent_test: Targeted weakness drills vs unguided rollouts at equal tokens. The three entries are one paper; authors include DP proponents; only the abstract was checked.

claim: Twin study: practice reduces shared-environment and residual variance but not genetic variance; about 50% heritable overall.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Chess dropouts learn at the same rate per unit of practice but develop slower (de Bruin 2008); abstract only.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Chess-trained specialist transformers reach strong play by supervised learning on engine labels: 270M model 95.4% puzzles, Lichess blitz 2895 vs humans, 2299 tournament Elo; only 1.33% of puzzles in the training set (verified in the paper).
agent_test: Shows amortised search in weights; our scaffold cannot train, so compare it against a prompting-only baseline on the same puzzles.

claim: A general LLM without chess training is far weaker: GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct 66.5% puzzles, about 1755 Elo vs bots, vs 95.4% for the specialist.
agent_test: Baseline for a chess-puzzle test of the scaffold.

claim: Complete-game training data helps LLMs: ChessLLM reaches Elo 1788; long-round supervision +350 Elo over short-round; wins 61% vs Stockfish level 0 (verified in text).
agent_test: a20 and b16 are the same paper.

claim: Chess-trained LLMs can be brittle: some solve mate-in-N 70-75% but a self-play-trained model got 2.1%; verifier loops raised legal-move rate (50.8% to 95.3%) but lowered puzzle accuracy for ChessGPT-Base (38.6% to 18.7%).
agent_test: Test an external verifier step at equal tokens and check it does not reduce accuracy.

claim: Human-AI teaching: four grandmasters improved on AlphaZero-concept puzzles between phase 1 and phase 3 (+6 to +42 points); gain did not track rating; 8 of 13 concepts improved. No control group of unaided practice.
agent_test: Concept-targeted example sets vs random examples for the agent, equal token budget. The three entries are versions of one study.

claim: AI engines are poor models of human play but can be tuned: Maia move-match 50.8-52.9% vs Stockfish/Leela 33-46%.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Self-improvement loops for LLMs show gains: STaR GSM8K 36.6 to 68.8 (72.5 with rationalization), Reflexion HumanEval 91% vs 80%, LeMa GSM8K 83.5 vs 81.4, SPIN leaderboard 58.14 to 63.16. Caveat from gap search: without an external or oracle signal, intrinsic self-correction lowered accuracy (Huang 2024: Llama-2 GSM8K 62.0 to 36.5).
agent_test: STaR, LeMa and SPIN train weights; only Reflexion is scaffold-only. Test a Reflexion-style note memory at equal tokens.

claim: Curriculum choice matters: Voyager random curriculum cut discovered items by 93%; PLR gave 76% test return gain; Skill-it beat uniform sampling.
agent_test: Order tasks by estimated weakness vs random order at equal tokens.

claim: Adaptive test-time compute beats best-of-N by over 4x efficiency; a smaller model beat a 14x larger one in matched FLOPs where it had non-trivial success.
agent_test: Adaptive per-item budget vs fixed budget at equal total tokens.

claim: AI-feedback practice platforms in medical training show gains: MedSimAI OSCE history 82.8 to 88.8 (d=0.75) at one site, none at another; CPX-MATE repeat score +1.67; HypoCompass +11.7%.
agent_test: Background; human-facing, small, uncontrolled.

claim: AI-assisted practice in music: self-regulated learning mediated AI practice to performance (indirect effect .183); observational SEM, not causal.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: The size of the DP effect depends on what counts as DP: Ericsson and Harwell 2019 (k=8) r=.56 (31.4%) vs Macnamara 2014 r=.38 (14.4%) vs Miller 2019 r=.40 (16.0%).
agent_test: Define the agent's 'practice' operationally before any test.

claim: Carlsen reached the top with fewer years since starting (18 vs mean 24.6 for the next ten), but rank vs years across the top ten was not significant (r=-0.21).
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Prompt-only gains across episodes exist (Reflexion 130/134 ALFWorld tasks in 12 trials; ExpeL 59% ALFWorld; AWM +24.6% / +51.1% relative) but depend on a reliable success signal, and iterative self-improvement saturates in a few rounds.
agent_test: Run repeated episodes with note memory vs none at equal tokens; plot gain per round; expect a plateau within about 3 to 6 rounds.

claim: Self-correction without an external check does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0); an external sound verifier lifts Blocksworld from 40/100 to 88/100 while an LLM verifier gives 55/100.
agent_test: Compare self-verifier vs tool or rule verifier on the same items; log the self-verifier false-positive rate.

claim: Verifier help is bounded by candidate quality: Blocks World 82% and Logistics 70% with a sound verifier, but about 10% on obfuscated Mystery Blocks World.
agent_test: Stratify tasks by base solve rate; expect verifier gain near zero where base rate is near zero.

claim: Adaptive curriculum beats random and easy-to-hard ordering at equal budget, but the gain shrinks with a stronger base model (SEC: 3B Countdown OOD 0.48 to 0.54; 7B 0.512 to 0.514), and easy-first ordering can be worse than random.
agent_test: A prompt-only test of weakness-ordered vs random task order at equal tokens is still missing.

claim: Scaffold or practice benefit has a ceiling: Self-Refine +0.2 on code optimisation where base is 92.9 and 0 on math; CoT helps mainly on math and symbolic items; Burgoyne chess ability effect r=.32 (lower skill) vs .14 (higher), age-confounded.
agent_test: Measure scaffold gain against base-model solve rate across at least three model strengths.

claim: Teacher guidance is not shown to add beyond goal plus feedback: deliberate practice r=.56 (k=8) vs purposeful practice r=.51 (k=6), difference p=.64.
agent_test: Three-arm ablation for an agent: goal only, goal plus feedback, goal plus feedback plus coach-model guidance.

claim: Experience must be new to help: ExpeL extracting insights only from its few-shot examples gave no gain over ReAct, and random retrieval of past trajectories lost clearly to task-similar retrieval.
agent_test: Random-example control vs similar-example retrieval at equal tokens.

claim: Southwick 2026 3.61x learning-efficiency result could not be checked for confounding by motivation or prior rating; full text unavailable.
agent_test: Read the supplement when accessible.
